changes._why: NULLS LAST still ranks a NULL first in a department whose salaries are all NULL; the salaries not recorded are left out, as Claude first proposed
request: Each department head is told who their best-paid employee is; ties are all reported, ordered by `EMPLOYEE_ID`.
An employee with no department, or no salary recorded, is left out, as the correlated solution leaves them out; HR_EMPLOYEES_B_09 lists the salaries not recorded.
changes.sql:
SELECT DEPARTMENT_ID, EMPLOYEE_ID, LAST_NAME, SALARY
FROM (SELECT e.*, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY DEPARTMENT_ID ORDER BY SALARY DESC) AS RNK
      FROM EMPLOYEES e
      WHERE DEPARTMENT_ID IS NOT NULL
        AND SALARY IS NOT NULL)
WHERE RNK = 1
ORDER BY DEPARTMENT_ID ASC, EMPLOYEE_ID ASC

changes._why: NULLS LAST still puts NULLs among the top three where a department has fewer than three salary levels; they are left out
request: Ahead of the bonus round, each department head wants the three highest salaries of the department and everyone who earns one of them, ties included.
Salaries not recorded are left out, so they never take a rank; the people of one rank are ordered by `EMPLOYEE_ID`.
changes.sql:
SELECT DEPARTMENT_ID, EMPLOYEE_ID, LAST_NAME, SALARY, RNK
FROM (SELECT e.*, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY DEPARTMENT_ID ORDER BY SALARY DESC) AS RNK
      FROM EMPLOYEES e
      WHERE DEPARTMENT_ID IS NOT NULL
        AND SALARY IS NOT NULL)
WHERE RNK <= 3
ORDER BY DEPARTMENT_ID ASC, RNK ASC, EMPLOYEE_ID ASC

changes._why: as HR_EMPLOYEES_A_02: the salaries not recorded are left out rather than ranked last
request: Each regional director is told who the best-paid people in their region are: the three highest salaries, ties included, ordered by last name and `EMPLOYEE_ID`.
Salaries not recorded are left out, so they never take a rank.
changes.sql:
SELECT REGION_NAME, EMPLOYEE_ID, LAST_NAME, JOB_TITLE, SALARY, RNK
FROM (SELECT v.*, DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY REGION_NAME ORDER BY SALARY DESC) AS RNK
      FROM EMP_DETAILS_VIEW v
      WHERE SALARY IS NOT NULL)
WHERE RNK <= 3
ORDER BY REGION_NAME ASC, RNK ASC, LAST_NAME ASC, EMPLOYEE_ID ASC

changes._why: the current position's start is inferred from the trigger, not recorded; the request says so
request: An employee asks HR for their record: every position they have held, the current one included, in date order.

The schema records no start for the current position, so the exercise infers one: the day after the last `END_DATE` of the history, which the trigger writes when the job changes, or `HIRE_DATE` if there is none; the current one, with no end, comes last on a tie.
